title: sole of the foot

chart.description: The sole of the foot and the plantar surface of the toes, seen from below. u: distance across the sole (cm) from its long axis (the line from the centre of the heel to the web between the second and third toes), positive towards the lateral (little-toe) side, negative towards the medial (great-toe) side. v: distance along the sole (cm) from the plantar margin of the web between the second and third toes, positive proximal (towards the heel), negative distal (along the toes). d: depth below the plantar skin (cm).

configurations.label: foot relaxed, sole turned to the practitioner

landmarks.label: plantar margin of the web between the second and third toes
back of the heel, on the long axis of the sole
deepest point of the depression in the front of the sole when the toes are curled
landmarks.palpation: Ask the patient to curl the toes: a hollow appears in the front of the sole, behind the pads of the second and third metatarsal heads, about a third of the way from the web between the second and third toes to the back of the heel.

landmarks.label: plantar pad over the head of the first metatarsal
plantar pad over the head of the fifth metatarsal
centre of the plantar crease of the distal interphalangeal joint of the second toe
landmarks.palpation: Flex the second toe: the distal of its two plantar creases.

landmarks.label: tip of the second toe (plantar pulp)

structures.label: common plantar digital nerve of the second interspace
common plantar digital artery of the second interspace
deep plantar arterial arch (at the bases of the metatarsals)

description: The sole. The plantar skin is thick, and over the heel and the ball of the foot a fibro-fatty pad lies beneath it; the plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity to the toes. Deep to it lie flexor digitorum brevis, the long flexor tendons with the lumbricals, and the interossei between the metatarsals. The medial and lateral plantar nerves and vessels run forward from the heel; the deep plantar arch crosses the bases of the metatarsals, and the common plantar digital nerves and arteries run in the interspaces towards the webs, superficial to the deep transverse metatarsal ligaments. A needle passing straight through an interspace reaches the dorsum.

sources.title: General regional anatomy of the sole of the foot (standard anatomy texts)
sources.note: Topography only; no third-party geometry or images were used.

review.notes: Positions and depths are illustrative approximations of a reference adult written for simulation. They are not measurements or an atlas and are not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.
